plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A long-lived perennial producing large, fragrant, often double blooms atop sturdy stems with glossy, deeply lobed foliage. A classic cottage garden favorite and a symbol of prosperity in Chinese culture.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Siberia, Mongolia, and northern China; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Some peony plants can live and bloom for over 100 years, and ants are often seen on the buds feeding on nectar, though they are not required for blooming.

plants.name: Iris germanica
plants.description: A rhizomatous perennial with sword-shaped gray-green leaves and showy flowers featuring three upright standards, three drooping falls, and a fuzzy 'beard' that guides pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (May to early June in temperate Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Hybrid of Mediterranean origin; cultivated throughout Europe, North America, and temperate Asia
plants.funFact: The iris is named after the Greek goddess of the rainbow, Iris, reflecting the enormous range of colors found in the genus. Its dried rhizomes, called orris root, are used in perfumery.

plants.name: Rosa rugosa
plants.description: A tough, hardy shrub with wrinkled, dark green leaves, thorny stems, and fragrant single or double flowers, followed by large red-orange hips rich in vitamin C.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring through summer, with peak bloom in late May to June
plants.location: Native to coastal eastern Asia (Japan, Korea, northeastern China); naturalized on beaches and dunes in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Rugosa roses thrive in salty sea spray and sandy soil, and are so vigorous they are considered invasive along some European and North American coastlines.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A graceful tree with fern-like foliage that erupts into clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, carpeting the ground beneath when they fall.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June); in the Southern Hemisphere it blooms in October to November
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in Mexico, California, Florida, the Mediterranean, and parts of Africa
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, known as the 'Jacaranda City,' tens of thousands of trees bloom at once, and in Mexico City the bloom marks the start of the rainy season.
